bluf: Mockingbird Marketing is a Seattle law firm marketing agency selling SEO, advertising, web design and business intelligence to small firms on transparent terms, with results measured in consultations, clients and revenue. The record shows a house going quiet: the latest capture is September 2025 and sitemap content stops in April 2025. The one thing a rival should know: it sells paid search and runs no Google ads, its public book is one client, and the Monsoon read puts it at Landfall, displacement 78.3. It is very likely, with moderate confidence, undercut on price and outpaced on AI, where it scores 0.
doing:
The positioning line, in the record's words: a law firm marketing agency selling transparent, no strings service and measuring marketing by consultations, clients and revenue rather than raw leads. In plain words: a small legal SEO shop selling honesty and outcome reporting, not scale. The headline claim is thin, a Google Premier Partner badge cited on its careers page, and the prominence signals are community rather than commercial: legal community events, a legal marketing podcast, a December 2022 ChatGPT, SEO and ethics webinar and a January 2023 PILMMA mastermind.

SEO leads at score 3: the homepage pitches smart, savvy SEO for law firms and most case studies are SEO experiments. Four core lines sit at score 2: Content & Digital PR (case studies on PR link building and a year of link building), Data & Measurement (reporting on consultations, clients and revenue instead of lead counts), Paid Search (AdWords, YouTube and Facebook, with Smart Bidding and Google versus Microsoft case studies) and Web & Product (redesign, site launch, rebuild and hosting case studies). The record lists no proprietary product and one partner, Google Premier Partner; AI Search / GEO and AI Automation / Agents score 0.

The AI posture field is null: an agency that ran a ChatGPT and ethics webinar in December 2022 shows no AI line in 2026, and the Horus read scores P1 absent. Pricing signals are terms, not prices: no long term contracts, no hidden data or blocked accounts, a pledge not to work with a client's competitors; no public pricing model shows (P5 unknown).

The record lists no moves, news, case study entries or jobs; the status note says the latest capture is September 2025 and sitemap content stops in April 2025, no closure or merger signal but no dated activity either. Conspicuously absent for its kind: a Local Services Ads line (P3 absent), any AI line, and any ad of its own.
clients:
The client type is SMB law firms; the verticals listed are personal injury, family, immigration, criminal defense, estate planning and probate, and mass torts. The home market is the US from a Seattle office.

The book on record is one name, and for once it is observed rather than inferred: Choquette Law Firm, from a case study slug reading website redesign, which the record reads as web build and platform, giving a mix read of web 1.0 on one case. No other client is named: the SEO experiments, link building and Smart Bidding case studies the capability notes cite carry no client names into the record, so the evidence of who buys the SEO it leads with is absent rather than thin. Named only is 0 of 1, shared is 0, and no press release, job or news item adds a name.

The rest of who it serves must be read from the verticals and the events: mass torts and personal injury firms sit in the vertical list, and the PILMMA mastermind and the legal community events point at the small firm marketing circuit rather than any named account.

What the base needs next, tied to the edition: small firms buying SEO, link building and paid search sit where KJ6 (The agency middle is being hollowed out) removes hours, so it is likely, with low confidence given one named client, that its firms ask for consultation and revenue reporting that proves the spend, which the P4 making read says Mockingbird supplies, and a roughly even chance that the same firms ask for AI search visibility, which the record shows it does not sell at all.

openings:
The strongest opening is price on a quiet house. The Monsoon read puts displacement at 78.3, Landfall, on an SMB book buying SEO and web hours, no public pricing model shows (P5 unknown), and the sitemap has not moved since April 2025: it is very likely, with moderate confidence, that an offshore delivered or outcome priced rival undercuts Mockingbird while it is not publishing. The falsifier: a sitemap update, a new case study or a price page at mockingbird.marketing at the next compile.

Second, the contradiction. It sells paid search and runs no Google ads of its own, the only tested line and it fails: a rival who runs its own ads wins the advertising line, likely with moderate confidence.

Third, AI. AI Search / GEO scores 0, the AI posture is null, P1 and P8 are absent and no feed, schema or entity work shows (P2 absent): every immigration, family or injury firm asking about AI answers is contestable, and it is almost certain, on this record, that Mockingbird has no answer to bring. Its defensible ground is the transparency pledge and the revenue reporting (P4 making), which a rival must match.
